newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Nov 29.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 51.3 percent rise in its turnover during the week ending November 29 on renewed buyer interest for wheat contracts and the central bank short-term bonds.
Total weekly turnover jumped to 51.431 million dinars ($10.2 million) from 33.99 million dinars a week ago. The number of transactions remained almost unchanged, slipping to 172 from 173.

"The BSE turnover rose on renewed demand for the central bank bonds and wheat contracts ahead of December 2, the closing date for the securities sale," head of the BSE trading activities Gordana Dostanic told Reuters.
The bourse spokesman Milko Stimac said it was mainly the hedgers -- flour mills -- who bought the contracts ahead of the deadline.
The bourse officials expected from the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency -- the contracts' issuer -- to soon announce a new round of sale under slightly revised conditions.
Except for the wheat contracts and the central bank bonds, trade on the Belgrade bourse remained under the pressure of tight market liquidity.
"Liquidity is very low and most of the activity is based on revolving old borrowing," one trader said.
Analysts cautioned that revolving became a dominant feature of market activity.

"Nevertheless, interest rates on those deals rise even though it is always the same amount of capital turning around. And the initial value of this capital is symbolic and multiplies unrealistically," said an analyst who asked not to be named.
The analyst feared the situation may even bring to a market crash and said problems could be avoided by a dinar devaluation only.
For the week ending November 29, the BSE reported the following details:
*Commercial paper accounted fo 18.194 million dinars in 130 transactions.
*Treasury bills were traded 28 times for a volume of 3.358 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent.
* Central bank short-term bonds accounted for 15 million dinars of the total weekly turnover and for only one deal.
* There were 11 deals in wheat selling forward contracts worth 14.579 million dinars. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
